summary: Edward Clive Bayley (1821–1884) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and East India Company College (~1840–1842). In 1842, he took up a post with the Indian Civil Service.

Edward Conze (1904–1979) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Tübingen, Heidelberg, Kiel, Hamburg, Bonn, and Cologne (Ph.D.), he studied under Max Scheler and Max Walleser. He held posts at London, Wisconsin-Madison, Washington, UC Berkeley, and Lancaster.

Edward Delavan Perry (1854–1938) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his A.B. at Columbia University (~1871–1875) and Dr. phil. at the University of Tübingen (~1877–1879), later serving as Jay Professor at Columbia University (1891–1931).

Edward Denison Ross (1871–1940) worked in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UCL and under Theodor Nöldeke at Strasbourg. His posts included UCL, Aliah University, University of Calcutta, the British Museum, and SOAS.

Edward Elbridge Salisbury (1814–1901) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Yale and in Europe under Woolsey, de Sacy, de Tassy, Bopp, Burnouf, and Lassen. He served as professor at Yale (1841–1854) and as president of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed doctoral research under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994). He held an academic post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett (1971–) is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his Ph.D. at UCLA (~1996–2001) under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, with postdoctoral mentoring from Anna Szabolcsi. He held research assistant posts at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

Edward Granville Browne (1862–1926) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge and St Bartholomew's under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell. He served as lecturer in Persian and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Edward H. Schafer (1913–1991) was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Harvard. He spent his career at UC Berkeley (~1947–1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Hamilton Johnston (1885–1942) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell, served in the Indian Civil Service (~1908–1924), and later held a professorship at the University of Oxford (~1937–1942).

Edward Joseph Thomas (1869–1958) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet and at the University of Cambridge, where he served as Dean of the Oriental Languages Department (~1909–1939).

Edward S. Casey (1939–) is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern (Ph.D.), and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UCSB and Yale before serving as faculty and dean at Stony Brook University (~1978).

Edward Said (1935–2003) was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. After attending Princeton University and Harvard University, he served as a professor of English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University from ~1963 to 2003.

Edward Sapir (1884–1939) was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Wilhelm Wundt and Franz Boas. He served at the Geological Survey of Canada (~1910–1925) and held academic posts at the University of Chicago and Yale University.

Edward Upham (1776–1834) was a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held posts as a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland and fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

Edward Vernon Arnold (1857–1926) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1880–1884), and served as a professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).

Edward Washburn Hopkins (1857–1932) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Columbia and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at Columbia, Bryn Mawr College, and Yale University, succeeding William Dwight Whitney.

Edward Winslow Bastian is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, studied with traditional teachers Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo, and researched at Banaras Hindu University.

Edwin Arnold (1832–1904) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology educated at King's College London and Oxford. He served as Principal of Deccan College (1856), fellow at the University of Mumbai, and guest lecturer at Keio University.

Edwin F. Bryant (1957–) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1991–1997). He taught at Harvard University (~1998–2003) and served as Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University (~2003).
